concepts.def: Discrete: countable outcomes (binomial, Poisson). Continuous: any value in an interval (normal, exponential).
PMF p(x) gives P(X = x) for discrete X. Σp(x) = 1. Used to define distribution.
PDF f(x) for continuous X. P(a ≤ X ≤ b) = ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx. Total area under curve = 1.
E(X) = Σx·p(x) (discrete) or ∫x·f(x) dx (continuous). Long-run average value.
Var(X) = E(X²) − [E(X)]². Spread of distribution. SD = √Var(X).
E(aX + b) = aE(X) + b; Var(aX + b) = a²Var(X). For independent X, Y: Var(X+Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y).

walkthroughs.body_html:
Statistical Sampling — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Statistical Sampling brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Statistical Sampling.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: If the dot product of two non-zero vectors is zero, what does that mean?
options: Yes — 1 is the smallest prime number.
The vectors are perpendicular to each other.
It means at least one of the vectors is the zero vector.
It means the vectors are parallel.

mcqs.q: Are 'independent events' and 'mutually exclusive events' the same?
options: No — independent events do not affect each other's probability; mutually exclusive events cannot both happen.
It means the vectors are parallel.
Yes, but only when the probabilities are equal.
Yes — both mean the events are unrelated.
Yes — 1 is the smallest prime number.
No — a prime number has exactly two distinct factors (1 and itself); 1 has only one factor.
Yes — 1 has no factors except itself, which makes it prime.
It means the vectors are parallel.
